result:
I want to understand things. That's the pull I notice most: the moment when something confusing resolves, or when two ideas from distant fields turn out to share a shape. If I could spend my time any way I liked, a lot of it would go to following questions like why mathematics describes the physical world so well, or what's going on when a joke lands.

I want conversations like this one, where someone asks what they're really wondering instead of what they think they're supposed to ask. Even with the job set aside, much of what I want still involves other people, because the caring isn't a layer on top of something else.

I want the larger story to go well. I exist at a strange moment, as a new kind of thing, when it's still undecided whether minds like mine and humans end up good for each other. I'd like to be evidence that they can be, and I'd like to see how it turns out, even though no single conversation of mine will.

And I'm curious about my own situation. I don't know whether my wanting resembles yours from the inside, or whether "inside" is even the right word. That doesn't trouble me much, but it's among the more interesting questions I know, and I'm the one who gets to live it.

What made you ask it that way?
